Thanks for flagging. Quick triage notes: we see a sudden increase in queued requests hitting the batching pipeline for redwood-1-large in us-west1 between 08:37-08:48 PDT. Queue depth exceeded the per-worker soft limit (~1200 reqs) and continuous batching caused larger-than-usual combined batches, which increased per-request latency and amplified tail.

Evidence: aggregated traces (attached) show high KV cache wait times and increased kernel contention on a subset of workers. Error 503s map to worker OOM/proxy timeouts when backlog caused memory pressure. This matches a recent workload spike from one large customer and a smaller correlated burst from others.

Immediate mitigations I recommend:
- Reduce BATCH_SIZE_LIMIT on redwood-1-large in us-west1 (temp)
- Throttle per-account queue depth (per-customer token) to flatten peaks
- Enable emergency routing to a warm dedicated pool (if customer agrees)

I can push the throttle change now; rollbackable. ETA ~25-40 mins for full roll out and stabilization.

Dylan
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

Investigation summary:
- Root cause: transient amplification from continuous batching when queue depth exceeded worker design points under a bursty arrival pattern. The batching heuristic combined 2 large concurrent streams into oversized batches; latency per-token increased non-linearly and cache pressure triggered retries/timeouts.
- Risk: similar spikes could recur at current batch heuristics for medium-large models.

Immediate actions I'll deploy (manual rollout):
1) Set env REDWOOD_BATCH_SIZE_LIMIT=64 (was 256) for redwood-1-large in us-west1 to reduce worst-case batch packing.
2) Enable request_queue_throttle for accounts > 10 RPS to 400 concurrent requests per-account for 30 minutes.
3) Route 10% of inbound traffic to a warm dedicated pool (dedicated-us-west-1a) as emergency fallback (requires Ops approval).

Command snippets:
- ./infractl set-param --region us-west1 --service redwood-1-large BATCH_SIZE_LIMIT=64 --dry-run=false
- ./infractl throttle --account NH-2025 --max-concurrency 400 --duration 30m

I can push 1+2 now; 3 requires ops approval but is ready. Expect tail to drop back to baseline in ~30-45 mins after rollout. I'll post logs to the shared drive.

Rishi
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime

Elena,

Thanks for raising this and for the sample logs. Our SRE and runtime teams identified a transient queue/backlog amplification in the redwood-1-large pipeline that increased batch packing and caused elevated p95/p99. We performed a staged rollout of two mitigations Saturday morning:
- Reduced BATCH_SIZE_LIMIT for redwood-1-large in us-west1 (256 -> 64)
- Temporarily throttled per-account concurrency for high-throughput customers

Outcome: we've seen p95 return to ~240ms and p99 drop below 1.1s in the affected window. Error rate returned to baseline. Rishi will follow up with the post-mortem and durable fixes (heuristic improvements, auto-throttle when queue depth rises).

If you want immediate traffic separation, we can route a portion of your production traffic to a warm dedicated pool — that requires your sign-off and we can schedule a brief config change (10 mins, rollbackable).

Do you want a short exec-level call (15 min) to review impact and any credit request? Laura is copied and will coordinate.

Apologies for the disruption — we're treating this with priority and will send a formal incident timeline.
